title: Neural Agent Compiler: Learning to Schedule Soft Dependencies
abstract: arXiv:2611.29262v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model agents accomplish complex tasks by coordinating multiple reasoning steps and tool operations, which form dependencies among their operations. Existing orchestration methods primarily consider hard dependencies that determine when an operation can legally begin, but overlook soft dependencies, i.e., information that is not required for execution but may improve an already executable operation. We identify soft-dependency scheduling as an important problem in agent execution. To this end, we introduce Neural Agent Compiler (NAC), a learned scheduler that predicts the task-quality and resource consequences of three execution modes and selects the highest-utility legal mode at a scheduling boundary. NAC represents the executable continuation, pending information event, and resource state in a shared memory, and uses a utility function to adapt the consequence predictions to different resource preferences. translated_title: 神经智能体编译器：学习调度软依赖
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型智能体通过协调多个推理步骤和工具操作来完成复杂任务，这些步骤和操作之间形成了依赖关系。现有的编排方法主要考虑硬依赖（即决定操作何时可以合法开始的关系），但忽略了软依赖，即那些并非执行所必需、但可能改进已可执行操作的信息。我们将软依赖调度确定为智能体执行中的一个重要问题。为此，我们提出了神经智能体编译器（NAC），这是一个学习型调度器，它能够预测三种执行模式对任务质量和资源的影响，并在调度边界处选择效用最高的合法模式。NAC 在共享内存中表示可执行的后续操作、待处理的信息事件和资源状态，并使用效用函数使后果预测适应不同的资源偏好。在 AppWorld
tldr: 该论文提出神经智能体编译器（NAC），一种学习型调度器，通过预测三种执行模式对任务质量和资源的后果，在调度边界选择效用最高的合法执行模式，从而首次将智能体执行中的软依赖调度作为重要问题加以解决。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Neural Agent Compiler (NAC), a learned scheduler that predicts the task-quality and resource consequences of three execution modes and selects the highest-utility legal mode at scheduling boundaries, addressing soft-dependency scheduling as an important problem in agent execution.
